subject: Clarifying jurisdictional constraints + IP safelist requirements for Private Endpoint
messages:
From: Alice Chan <alice.chan@novamed.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@novamed.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Private deployment — legal/jurisdiction question + allowlist needs

Hi Stephanie / Marissa,

Thanks again for walking us through the Private deployment options. Our legal and infra teams want to confirm two things before we move forward with a POC:

1) Jurisdictional constraint: NovaMed needs assurance that control-plane telemetry and any outage notifications will not cross US borders. For EU customers/data we need confirmation of control-plane egress behavior and whether notifications or health pings can be scoped to eu-only endpoints.

2) IP allowlisting: our networking team requires a consolidated list of stable outbound IPs (or clearly documented rotation strategy) we can add to our firewall. If there are any DNS-based fallbacks or hostnames we must allow (SNI/TLS), please list them. Also need a short explanation of how certificate validation and SNI will be observed from our egress proxy.

Attached is NovaMed's outline of compliance requirements (novamed-egress-requirements.pdf). Can you provide an evidence bundle and a concise network checklist we can hand to our infra team?

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Chan
Head of Cloud Ops — NovaMed
Attachment: novamed-egress-requirements.pdf (application/pdf, 285 KB)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chan <alice.chan@novamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 16:35:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deployment — legal/jurisdiction question + allowlist needs

Hi Alice —

Appreciate the clear ask and the PDF. High-level answers up front:
- Control-plane telemetry/notifications: we can restrict control-plane callbacks to EU control-plane endpoints for customers selecting the EU private plane. The Private deployment option supports region-scoped control planes; we'll capture evidence of egress destinations.
- IP allowlisting: we will provide a stable set of public IPs for the control-plane egress and a recommended set for optional runtime telemetry. Where IP rotation is unavoidable (ephemeral NAT pools), we'll document the rotation window and the mechanized approach (e.g., DNS entries + short TTL).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Marissa will prepare a concise network checklist (IPs, ports, FQDNs, SNI notes) and an evidence CSV mapping which flows are mandatory vs optional.
2) Laura — can you confirm whether we need to propose an SLA exception or a contractual data localization clause for NovaMed? That will determine whether we escalate to Legal for a tailored appendix.

Marissa — please include snippets for firewall ACLs (fw-snippets.txt) and an annex describing how we handle SNI/TLS visibility with typical egress proxies (e.g., explicit SNI allow vs full TLS termination).

I'll follow up with a short summary for Alice to share with her infra team.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chan <alice.chan@novamed.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 17:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deployment — legal/jurisdiction question + allowlist needs

Hi Alice — attaching the technical checklist and IP list for the EU-scoped private control plane. See attached CSV (redwood-egress-ip-list.csv) and a short fw-snippets.txt with example ACL entries you can paste into your firewall appliance.

Key items (summary):
- Required outbound destinations (control plane, config fetch, health):
  • 18.199.128.0/22  (control-plane-egress-1) — static pool (monthly rotation notice)
  • 3.64.20.0/24     (control-plane-egress-2) — static pool (quarterly announce)
  • control.eu.redwood-inference.com (CNAME -> dynamic NAT range) — for fallback if you prefer FQDN allowlist

- Ports/Protocols:
  • TCP 443 (HTTPS) mandatory for all control-plane traffic
  • TCP 80 (optional) only for initial health probes if TLS termination is handled upstream (we recommend blocking 80 and allowing 443 only)
  • Outbound DNS (UDP/TCP 53) required if you allow FQDNs rather than IPs

- SNI/TLS:
  • We serve with a Redwood wildcard cert; SNI is preserved. If your egress proxy performs TLS interception, you must install a CA that allows interception — in that case, certificate pinning will fail. Our checklist notes how to confirm TLS passthrough (look for the SNI value control.eu.redwood-inference.com).

- Rotation & Evidence:
  • Where IPs are marked as "static pool" we will notify NovaMed 10 business days prior to rotation. For ephemeral pools (not in the CSV) we provide a documented rotation window and publish a JSON feed with current active addresses (each feed entry includes a valid_from timestamp).

- Operational advice:
  • If you cannot rely on DNS allowlist, allow both the IP pools above and control.eu.redwood-inference.com.
  • For maximum assurance, use a dedicated NAT gateway with source NAT mapping to a fixed public IP controlled by NovaMed — we can support routing the runtime through a customer-managed NAT where desired (adds complexity).

Attachments: redwood-egress-ip-list.csv (text/csv), fw-snippets.txt (text/plain)
